title: Telemetry-driven kernel selector and prefill/decode coordination for MIG co-located workloads
creator: Rohan Patel
description: Problem: In mixed-MIG deployments we observe tail latency regressions and costly GPU-clock thrashing when kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduling are decided without slice-aware telemetry. This ticket implements a telemetry-driven heuristic kernel selector and a lightweight coordinator that assigns prefill and decode phases to MIG slices to maximize utilization and minimize clock transitions. Goals: (1) reduce p95 decode latency for seq_len 512 workloads on H100 by >=15%, (2) improve aggregate throughput for mixed-sequence workloads on shared MIG fleets by >=12%, (3) eliminate >80% of unnecessary clock changes across slices under steady-state workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry pipeline collects per-MIG-slice metrics (avg_clock_mhz, temp_c, nvlink_bw, gpu_util_pct, token_density) every 5s
Kernel selector returns stable choice for 95% of requests under similar token_density and sequence length (no oscillation causing clock changes)
End-to-end benchmark: p95 decode latency reduction >=15% for H100 seq_len 512 (compared to baseline runtime-1.19 config)
Throughput improvement >=12% for mixed short/long sequence mix (10% long, 90% short) across L40S/A10 hetero fleets
Documented rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback if customer_impact becomes high
plan: Phase 1: Telemetry ingestion — extend runtime exporter to emit per-MIG-slice metrics and token_density (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4219)
Phase 2: Heuristic kernel selector — lightweight rule engine that picks between FlashAttention, TiledAttn, and QuantizedPrim kernels using recent slice telemetry and request-level signals
Phase 3: Prefill/Decode coordinator — affinity policy that pins prefill work to higher-clock slices and decode to KV-affine slices, with optional token-density-based swap
Phase 4: Canary rollout on dedicated testfleet (one region) with dashboarding and automatic fallback to existing kernel selector
Phase 5: Bake and ship with runtime-1.20 and document knobs in Console
experiments: Experiment A (H100): Compare kernel selector variants (static, recent-avg telemetry, exponential-weighted telemetry) on 512/2048 mixed seq workload. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, clock-change-rate, GPU hours.
Experiment B (L40S/A10 hetero): Measure throughput variance when prefill pinned to 2x higher-clock slices vs round-robin across MIG slices under token-dense prompts.
Experiment C (Thermal): Inject synthetic temperature spikes to validate selector avoids aggressive clock ramps and triggers fallback kernel that is clock-steady.
Experiment D (KV-cache affinity): Evaluate decode latency when decode is scheduled on slice owning warm KV cache vs remote slice (cross-slice NVLink fetchs)
benchmarks: Baseline: runtime-1.19 - H100 - seq512 p95 decode = 92ms
Target: runtime-1.20 (this work) - H100 - seq512 p95 decode <= 78ms
Baseline mixed workload throughput: 1000 reqs/min -> Target >= 1120 reqs/min
